headline: Nov 2-3 overnight Russian barrage casualty/outage Kharkiv hospital struck, 73 injured, 226 patients evacuated
dek: Russia's overnight Nov 2-3 barrage (289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles, 59 cruise missiles per President Zelenskyy and Ukraine's Air Force) hit energy generation and substations in 10 oblasts and directly struck a city clinical hospital in Kharkiv's Nemyshlianskyi district at ~03:20, injuring 73…
sources: Al Jazeera; Ukrainska Pravda (Energy Ministry briefing); Hromadske (Ukrainian Air Force); Ukrinform (Prosecutor General); New Voice of Ukraine (Zhytomyr governor)
fault_line: Deliberate energy-war pressure on civilians vs military-supply targeting: is a hospital hit and an aid-site strike collateral damage in a grid campaign, or evidence the campaign itself targets civilian survival?

sections.what_happened: Russia's overnight Nov 2-3 barrage (289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles, 59 cruise missiles per President Zelenskyy and Ukraine's Air Force) hit energy generation and substations in 10 oblasts and directly struck a city clinical hospital in Kharkiv's Nemyshlianskyi district at ~03:20, injuring 73 people (patients, medical staff, nearby residents), shattering 1,000+ windows and forcing evacuation of 226 patients; in Dnipro 1 person was killed and 15 injured with a hospital damaged; the death toll at the Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia) humanitarian-aid distribution site rose to 29 with 48 still missing; Zhytomyr region had 180,000+ people without power Tuesday morning, emergency outages applied in Kyiv and five oblasts, and scheduled cuts exceeding 12 hours elsewhere. Russia's Defence Ministry says it targeted electricity facilities supplying the army and military factories; it has not commented on the hospital or aid-site strikes in the sources checked.
sections.what_verified: Hospital toll 73 corroborated across Al Jazeera, Ukrinform (Prosecutor General), Hromadske and Euromaidan/United24; barrage size and 9-10 oblast scope corroborated by Zelenskyy statement carried by Al Jazeera, Ukrainska Pravda (Energy Ministry) and Hromadske (Air Force); Zhytomyr 180,000 figure corroborated by NV (governor) and Al Jazeera. The FAB-250/UMPK-5R munition identification is preliminary per prosecutors, not confirmed. Aid-site toll 29/48 via ANI-syndicated Tribune/AP-linked reporting is single-family for that sub-claim and is carried as attributed, not independently corroborated in-window.
sections.what_disputed: Russia's Defence Ministry frames the night's targets as military-supplying electricity facilities (1400-02) and has offered no account of the hospital or aid-site strikes in the sources checked; casualty counts for the hospital rose through the morning (46 -> 62 -> 73), so the final toll should be treated as the prosecutors' latest figure, not an early wire number. The aid-site 29/48 figure rests on ANI-syndicated reporting and lacks a second declared-tier family in-window.
sections.why_matters: 289 drones, 59 missiles, 1 hospital: the night Russia hit Ukraine's grid and its wards on US election day — 73 injured in one hospital, 29 dead at an aid queue
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW PUBLICATION + MISSED CATCH-UP TO 1400-02 (Al Jazeera published 10:18Z = 14:18 , in-window; Ukrainska Pravda 11:14+02 = 13:14 and Hromadske 11:13+02 = 13:13 , previous window, absent from the 1400 items) -- Nov 2-3 overnight Russian barrage casualty/outage update: Kharkiv hospital struck, 73 injured, 226 patients evacuated; Dnipro 1 killed, 15 injured; Komyshuvakha aid-site toll 29 dead, 48 missing; energy sites in 10 oblasts, emergency outages, >12-hour scheduled cuts

totw_analysis: Our read: 289 drones, 59 missiles, 1 hospital: the night Russia hit Ukraine's grid and its wards on US election day — 73 injured in one hospital, 29 dead at an aid queue The fault line our audience is arguing over: Deliberate energy-war pressure on civilians vs military-supply targeting: is a hospital hit and an aid-site strike collateral damage in a grid campaign, or evidence the campaign itself targets civilian survival?
